text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Local dealers said the crown will be fixed closer to the market rate against the dollar and mark within a few days.
- Some banks said they have registered an increase in citizens' demand for hard currencies against the Slovak crown.
- Brokers said Slovak companies should turn to the stock market to obtain funds since it now offered much cheaper money compared with bank loans.
- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said it was not likely to join a common block of the other largest opposition parties before next year's parliamentary elections.

SME - The USA has said the failed Slovak referendum on NATO membership and direct presidential elections was a step back from the system of democratic elections carried out in Slovakia after the fall of communism in 1989.

- EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek on Thursday arrives on a one-day visit to Slovakia with a message of concern at the failure of a weekend referendum seen as a key test of democracy, western diplomats said.
- President Michal Kovac has still not officially accepted the resignation of Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik.
- Opposition parties have warned military neutrality will push Slovakia to international isolation.

PRAVDA - The Foreign Ministry has strictly rejected the U.S. criticism over the recent referendums in Slovakia, saying such statements were a misunderstanding and resulted from little knowledge of Slovakia's legal system.
- Jan Gabriel, President of the largest Slovak commercial bank VUB, said Slovak citizens should not feel a strong negative effect of the decline of the Czech crown.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Production of Slovakia's electrotechnic industry increased by 17.9 percent year-on-year in 1996, with the exports rising by 19.3 percent against 1995.
- Slovakia's largest isnsurer Slovenska Poistovna said it had posted a profit of 339.2 million crown in 1996.
